rulings.case: Serna v. Law Office of Joseph Onwuteaka, P.C.
rulings.rule: Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(1)(C) and 6(d) (as amended eff. 2009-12-01; electronic service still earned +3 days until 2016-12-01); 15 U.S.C. 1692k(d)
rulings.trigger_event: FDCPA violation under 1692i(a)(2) occurred when Serna was served with the state-court collection suit
rulings.service_method: Clerk notice of IFP denial by mail and electronic means (2011-08-15); trigger itself was service of state suit
rulings.filing_date: 2011-08-18 (original complaint 2011-08-12 with IFP application; refiled with fee 2011-08-18)
rulings.court_computed_deadline: 2011-08-14 is a Sunday so limitation ran to 2011-08-15 (Rule 6(a)(1)(A),(C)); 6(d) adds 3 days after the IFP-denial notice, so 2011-08-18
pin_cites: slip op. 14-15 (PDF pp. 14-15): date computation and Rule 6(d) application
slip op. 2 (PDF p. 2): filing dates August 12/15/18, 2011
rulings.notes: Mixed question: trigger is a substantive FDCPA accrual holding; computation is Rule 6(a) then 6(d). Dissent (Smith, J.) disputes the trigger, not the arithmetic. The court notes at its footnote 18 it need not decide tolling during IFP.

rulings.rule: Fed. R. Civ. P. 23(f) (14 days after order entered); Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(d); Fed. R. App. P. 26(c)
rulings.rule_version_in_force: FRCP 6 / FRAP 26 (2009 text with e-service +3 days), events Mar-Apr 2014
rulings.service_method: not stated in the opinion; court holds service is irrelevant because the period runs from entry
rulings.court_computed_deadline: not stated as a date; court counts 17 days after entry versus the 14-day limit (14 days from 2014-03-24 is 2014-04-07, by arithmetic not quoted from the opinion)
rulings.holding: untimely (petition dismissed); 6(d)/26(c) 3 days do not apply to deadlines running from entry of an order
pin_cites: slip op. PDF pp. 12-14: Rule 23(f) petition 17 days after entry; Rule 6(d)/26(c) inapplicable; citing Eastman v. First Data Corp., 736 F.3d 675, 677 (3d Cir. 2013)
rulings.notes: Cited authority Eastman (3d Cir.) agrees; no split on this point.

rulings.rule: 8 U.S.C. 1252(b)(1) (30 days after date of final order); Fed. R. App. P. 26(a), 26(c)
rulings.trigger_event: BIA decision denying motion to reconsider (final order)
rulings.service_method: BIA decision with cover letter (delivery method not stated); statute runs from date of order, not service
rulings.court_computed_deadline: 30 days from 2015-01-30 is Sunday 2015-03-01, so due Monday 2015-03-02 (FRAP 26(a))
rulings.holding: untimely; jurisdictional; Rule 26(c) 3 days apply only to periods triggered by service
rulings.notes: Cites Nahatchevska v. Ashcroft, 317 F.3d 1226, 1227 (10th Cir. 2003), same result.

rulings.case: Ultimate Appliance CC v. Kirby Co.
rulings.era: pre-2009 rules in force on the relevant dates (Sept-Dec 2008); decided after
rulings.rule_version_in_force: pre-2009-12-01 time computation (events 2008); opinion quotes the then-current Rule 26(c) "3 calendar days" text
rulings.service_method: electronic notice of the dismissal (per the opinion)
rulings.filing_date: 2008-12-02 (motion for extension of time to appeal)
rulings.court_computed_deadline: notice of appeal due 2008-10-30; extension motion due 2008-12-01
rulings.holding: untimely; no 3 extra days under Rule 6/26(c) because the Rule 4 clock runs from entry, not service
rulings.notes: Event dates are before the Dec. 1, 2009 amendments; the ruling date is after, but the court applies the rules in force on the event dates. Opinion collects same-result cases from 1st, 5th, 6th, 8th, Fed. Cir.

rulings.service_method: n/a (period runs from entry; electronic filing of the motion)
rulings.holding: untimely; e-filing deadline ends at midnight in the court time zone (Rule 6(a)(4)(A)); nunc pro tunc cannot extend

rulings.rule: 29 C.F.R. 1614.106(b) (15 days); Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(d) argued by analogy
rulings.rule_version_in_force: FRCP 6 (2009 text); administrative deadline events July 2010
rulings.trigger_event: receipt of Notice of Rejection of Formal Complaint (NORF)
rulings.service_method: hand delivery per counsel at oral argument (brief had said mail)
rulings.holding: untimely; Rule 6(d) argument waived, FRCP does not govern non-judicial proceeding, and hand delivery earns no 3 days
rulings.notes: Weak as an FRCP 6 validation case (administrative deadline); kept as a negative example for 6(d) scope.

rulings.case: LeGras v. Aetna Life Insurance Co.
rulings.rule: Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(1)(C) next-business-day method, adopted as ERISA federal common law for a 180-day plan appeal period
rulings.trigger_event: denial letter of long-term disability benefits
rulings.court_computed_deadline: 180th day is Saturday 2011-10-15; period continues to Monday 2011-10-17
rulings.notes: Contractual/ERISA period, so Rule 6(a) applies by federal common law, not by its own terms. Dissent (N.R. Smith, J.) says contract interpretation.

rulings.rule: 28 U.S.C. 2107(c); Fed. R. App. P. 4(a)(6) (14 days after reopening order entered)
rulings.rule_version_in_force: FRAP 4(a)(6) as in force Feb 2004 (before the 2005 amendment noted in the opinion)
rulings.trigger_event: district court order reopening the appeal period
rulings.service_method: order received by mail (dissent, 551 U.S. at 222)
rulings.court_computed_deadline: 2004-02-24 (14 days); the district court had wrongly said 2004-02-27
rulings.notes: Source is the official U.S. Reports volume from GPO, not CourtListener.
